title: You can hear a sloth bear eat from 185 m

scenes.headline: You can hear this bear eating 185 m away.
It rips open termite mounds and shuts its nostrils.
scenes.body: Closed nostrils keep out dust and insects while it feeds.

scenes.label: front teeth missing: a built-in straw
scenes.body: Adults lack the top two incisors, so they suck termites up like a vacuum, puffing loudly.
scenes.source: Smithsonian's National Zoo; Animal Diversity Web

scenes.headline: It's also the only bear that routinely carries its cubs on its back.
scenes.source: Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Red List

caption:
A feeding sloth bear can be heard up to 185 m away.

About 20,000 or fewer sloth bears remain in the wild, and numbers have fallen by 30 to 49% over the last 30 years.

Sources: Animal Diversity Web; Smithsonian's National Zoo; IUCN Red List. Photos: Ranthambore & Bor Tiger Reserve. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Sound-based hook that makes viewers imagine the noise, then explains the anatomy behind it; all-Indian sloth bear photos.
